newsitem.title: USA: Glickman declines comment on US corn/soy forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Glickman declines comment on US corn/soy forecasts.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman declined to comment on the accuracy of a recent private forecast of domestic corn and soybean production but said variations in estimates were to be expected.

"Until such time as you get to the end of September there are always variations in the analysis of the corn and bean crop. I don't think we've seen the last word on the total crop yet," Glickman said following a forum on rural issues.
Professional Farmers of America on Monday pegged the 1996 U.S. crop at 8.2 billion bushels, well below USDA's August forecast for 8.695 billion bushels.
The forecast was based largely on data compiled on a crop tour organized by Pro Farmer with participants including USDA analysts.
"I can't comment on the accuracy of those numbers. I'm just saying you will see some variations until the final crop numbers come out," he said.
Pro Farmer also projected U.S. soybean production at around 2.1 billion bushels, versus USDA's current projection of 2.3 billion.
Glickman also reiterated his opposition to restrictions on U.S. grain exports, despite strong domestic prices.
"The government is not in the position of restricting exports, I have said that over and over again. The market place will make that judgement and it has," he said.
